# Contributing

Thanks for helping curate this list. The process is deliberately mechanical so an
autonomous updater agent and humans can collaborate on the same file.

## The one rule

**Edit `data/papers.yaml`, never `README.md`.** The README is generated by
`python3 scripts/build_readme.py`. After editing the YAML, run the script and
commit both files.

## Adding an entry

Copy this template, fill every field you can, and use `null` (not a guess) for
anything unverified:

```yaml
- title: "Exact Paper Title"
  venue: "NeurIPS"        # or null
  year: 2025              # or null
  vhint: arxiv            # where you found it
  url: "https://..."      # canonical link, or null
  modes: [steerable]      # overton | steerable | distributional | all (multiple allowed)
  method: design_science  # empirical | design_science | na (surveys/position)
  track: cs               # cs | journals
  kind: method            # method | dataset | benchmark | survey | position
  blurb: "One neutral sentence on the contribution."
  conf: high              # high | medium | low (your classification confidence)
```

Classification guidance:
- **Empirical** = measures/audits/explains existing models; no novel artifact proposed.
- **Design science** = proposes and evaluates a novel artifact (algorithm, method, framework, dataset-as-artifact).
- **Modes** follow Sorensen et al., ICML 2024: Overton (range of views, no endorsement),
  steerable (adapts to a principal), distributional (matches population distribution).

Then: `python3 scripts/build_readme.py && git add -A && git commit -m "add: <title>"`.

## The updater agent

A scheduled agent refreshes the list bi-weekly (arXiv sweeps, upstream diffs, journal-track
hunting, link resolution). Its instructions live in `agents/update_brief.md` and each run
is logged under `agents/runs/`. If the agent misclassifies something, fix the YAML directly —
corrections beat complaints.
